# EU Funding News · Ullswater Investments — full text of recent articles

## €86 million for investment projects in Teruel through the 2026 FITE fund
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/teruel-investment-fund-fite-2026-86-million/
Date: 2026-11-25 · Category: Spain · Source: La Moncloa – Council of Ministers (https://www.lamoncloa.gob.es/consejodeministros/referencias/Paginas/2026/20261124-referencia-rueda-de-consejo-ministros.aspx)

Spain approves a €43 million direct grant to Aragon for the Teruel Investment Fund; the regional government matches it.

- Instrument: Royal Decree, Council of Ministers, 24 November 2026
- State contribution: €43 million
- Aragon contribution: €43 million (total €86 million)
- Minimum project cost: €125,000
- Eligible period: 1 January 2026 – 31 December 2029
- Project selection: Government of Aragon, after a report from the Government Delegation

The Spanish Government has approved a €43 million direct grant to Aragon for the 2026 Teruel Investment Fund (FITE). Aragon matches the State's contribution, bringing the fund to €86 million this year.
The fund supports projects that generate economic activity in the province of Teruel. Projects must cost at least €125,000, and eligible actions can run from 1 January 2026 to 31 December 2029. The Government of Aragon selects the projects.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Ullswater Investments analysis: FITE is one of Spain's main investment tools against depopulation. Companies planning industrial, agrifood or energy investments in Teruel should follow the regional selection process.

## Spanish Chamber of Commerce gets €1 million to manage ERDF and ESF+ programmes
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/spanish-chamber-commerce-erdf-esf-intermediate-body-grant/
Date: 2026-11-25 · Category: Spain · Source: La Moncloa – Council of Ministers (https://www.lamoncloa.gob.es/consejodeministros/referencias/Paginas/2026/20261124-referencia-rueda-de-consejo-ministros.aspx)

The direct grant covers the chamber's 2026 costs as an Intermediate Body of EU cohesion funds.

- Instrument: Royal Decree for a direct grant, 24 November 2026
- Amount: €1 million
- Budget: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business
- Covers: 2026 staff and material costs as an Intermediate Body for ERDF and ESF+

Spain's Government has renewed a €1 million direct grant to the Spanish Chamber of Commerce. The grant covers its 2026 staff and material costs as an Intermediate Body of the European Regional Development Fund and the European Social Fund Plus.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Ullswater Investments analysis: through the chamber network, these EU funds reach SMEs via programmes for digitalisation, internationalisation and employment, so keeping the Intermediate Body running keeps those programmes going.

## €492.2 million zero-interest loan for the SPAINSAT-NG III satellite
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/spainsat-ng-iii-492-million-loan-hisdesat/
Date: 2026-11-25 · Category: EIC, Defence & Equity · Source: La Moncloa – Council of Ministers (https://www.lamoncloa.gob.es/consejodeministros/referencias/Paginas/2026/20261124-referencia-rueda-de-consejo-ministros.aspx)

Spain's Ministry of Industry lends HISDESAT €492.2 million for its new secure communications satellite and reschedules the €808 million loan for SPAINSAT-NG I and II.

- Instrument: Royal Decree, Council of Ministers, 24 November 2026
- Beneficiary: HISDESAT
- Loan: €492.2 million, zero interest, no guarantees
- Covers: Development, manufacture, launch and entry into service
- Repayment: 2026–2030
- SPAINSAT-NG I/II: €808 million loan rescheduled to 2026–2039, no new public spending

Spain's Government has approved a €492.2 million direct loan, at zero interest and without guarantees, to the satellite operator HISDESAT for SPAINSAT-NG III. The loan covers the development, manufacture, launch and entry into service of this secure governmental communications satellite.
A second Royal Decree reschedules repayment of the €808 million loan for SPAINSAT-NG I and II to between 2026 and 2039, with no new public spending.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Ullswater Investments analysis: the programme keeps Spain's space and defence industry and its supply chain busy, and many of those suppliers also compete for European Defence Fund and EU space programme funding.

## Spain approves up to €1 billion in state guarantees to renew and decarbonise the merchant fleet
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/spain-state-guarantees-1-billion-merchant-fleet/
Date: 2026-11-25 · Category: Climate & Energy · Source: La Moncloa – Council of Ministers (https://www.lamoncloa.gob.es/consejodeministros/referencias/Paginas/2026/20261124-referencia-rueda-de-consejo-ministros.aspx)

The guarantees, available until 2029, are part of a Royal Decree-law on transport for 2027.

- Instrument: Royal Decree-law on transport for 2027, 24 November 2026
- Amount: State guarantees of up to €1 billion
- Available until: 2029
- Purpose: Building, buying or converting ships and decarbonising the merchant fleet

Spain's Government has approved state guarantees of up to €1 billion, available until 2029, to finance building, buying or converting ships and to decarbonise the merchant fleet. The measure is part of a Royal Decree-law on transport for 2027.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Ullswater Investments analysis: state guarantees make it easier for shipowners to raise financing for fleet renewal and low-emission vessels, which can be combined with EU funding for clean maritime technologies.

## Spain clears €40 million call for job-creating business projects in just transition areas
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/spain-just-transition-40-million-business-call/
Date: 2026-11-25 · Category: Spain · Source: La Moncloa – Council of Ministers (https://www.lamoncloa.gob.es/consejodeministros/referencias/Paginas/2026/20261124-referencia-rueda-de-consejo-ministros.aspx)

The Council of Ministers authorises the Just Transition Institute to launch its 2026 call for business projects in areas hit by the closure of coal mines and coal and nuclear power plants.

- Approved: Council of Ministers, 24 November 2026
- Managing body: Just Transition Institute (ITJ), Ministry for the Ecological Transition
- Maximum budget: €40 million
- Target: Job-creating business projects in just transition areas
- Minimum investment (small projects): Lowered from €30,000 to €6,000 (Order TED/1171/2026)
- Deadline: Call not yet published

Spain's Council of Ministers has authorised the Just Transition Institute to launch its 2026 call for business projects that create jobs in just transition areas, with a budget of up to €40 million. These are territories affected by the closure of coal mines, coal-fired power plants and nuclear plants.
The call follows a change to the regulatory bases approved in early November, which lowered the minimum investment for small projects from €30,000 to €6,000 and opened the scheme to smaller businesses and entrepreneurs.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Ullswater Investments analysis: just transition areas offer some of the most generous investment support in Spain. Companies planning to invest or expand there should prepare their projects now, because the call is expected to open soon.

## Spain adds €200 million to its FIEM credit line for SME exporters
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/spain-fiem-sme-line-200-million/
Date: 2026-11-25 · Category: Spain · Source: La Moncloa – Council of Ministers (https://www.lamoncloa.gob.es/consejodeministros/referencias/Paginas/2026/20261124-referencia-rueda-de-consejo-ministros.aspx)

The Council of Ministers lifts the FIEM line for SMEs and small export and investment projects from €400 million to €600 million, after a record year.

- Approved: Council of Ministers, 24 November 2026
- New allocation: €600 million (from €400 million)
- Maximum per operation: €10 million
- 2026 so far: 35 operations worth €68.7 million, a record year by amount
- Managed by: Secretary of State for Trade

Spain's Council of Ministers has increased the FIEM (Fund for the Internationalisation of Companies) line for SMEs and small export and investment projects by €200 million. The line's total allocation rises from €400 million to €600 million.
The line finances up to €10 million per operation. Demand has grown strongly: in 2026 it has already backed 35 operations worth €68.7 million, its best year by amount since it was created in 2017.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Ullswater Investments analysis: FIEM offers official financing to Spanish companies that sell goods and services or invest abroad. A larger SME line gives smaller exporters more room to finance projects in emerging markets.

## Spain backs battery assembly plants for the automotive sector in Valencia and Castile and León
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/spain-battery-assembly-automotive-valencia-castile-leon/
Date: 2026-11-25 · Category: Spain · Source: La Moncloa – Council of Ministers (https://www.lamoncloa.gob.es/consejodeministros/referencias/Paginas/2026/20261124-referencia-rueda-de-consejo-ministros.aspx)

Two Royal Decrees give €4 million to the Valencia region and €3 million to Castile and León, which must at least match the amounts.

- Instrument: Two Royal Decrees, Council of Ministers, 24 November 2026
- Ministry: Industry and Tourism
- Valencia region: €4 million
- Castile and León: €3 million
- Regional co-funding: At least equal: at least €14 million in total
- Regional instruments due by: 31 December 2027

Spain's Ministry of Industry and Tourism will grant €4 million to the Valencia region and €3 million to Castile and León to support battery plants and assembly lines for the automotive sector. Each region must at least match the State's contribution, so the two programmes will mobilise at least €14 million.
The regions have until the end of 2027 to set up their own support instruments for companies.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Ullswater Investments analysis: battery assembly is a key link in the electric-vehicle value chain. Automotive suppliers in both regions should watch for the regional calls that will channel this funding.

## Spain's €600m AI voucher: what it will fund and when it opens
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/spain-ai-voucher-600-million-what-smes-need-to-know/
Date: 2026-11-25 · Category: Spain · Source: La Moncloa – Plan IA360 (PDF) (https://www.lamoncloa.gob.es/presidente/actividades/Documents/2026/20260920%20Plan%20IA360.pdf)

Plan IA360's business AI voucher will fund AI services from European tech firms, not licences. A pilot comes in H1 2027 and the general call before end-2027.

- Instrument: Business AI voucher (Plan IA360, project 11)
- Budget: €600 million
- Funds: AI-based services and solutions from European technology companies
- Excludes: Mere subscriptions to licences
- Pilot: Regulatory design and controlled pilot, first half of 2027
- General call: Before the end of 2027
- Target: 25,000 companies transformed

The business AI voucher is project 11 of Plan IA360. It will finance AI-based services and solutions offered by European technology companies that use foundation models as an input and add their own value, such as development, integration, sector knowledge, data processing or process redesign.
Simple licence subscriptions are excluded: only services that transform the beneficiary's production processes qualify. The design foresees milestone-based payments, conditions on AI training for staff and on embedding AI in internal processes, a prior maturity diagnosis, a concrete use case and later measurement of productivity impact.
The voucher is linked to Red NEURONA and will subsidise the solutions that its centres offer to SMEs. The plan sets regulatory design and a controlled pilot in the first half of 2027, and a general call with €600 million before the end of 2027, with a target of 25,000 companies.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Ullswater Investments analysis: the voucher cannot be requested yet and no bases have been published. Technology providers should prepare concrete, measurable use cases now, since the voucher pays for process transformation and milestones rather than software licences.

## Madrid hosts the EIT Health Summit 2026 for the first time
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/madrid-hosts-eit-health-summit-2026/
Date: 2026-11-25 · Category: Health & Health Data · Source: Comunidad de Madrid (https://www.comunidad.madrid/notas-prensa/2026/11/24/comunidad-madrid-acoge-primera-vez-cumbre-importante-europa-innovacion-salud)

The summit, held on 24 and 25 November, marks ten years of EIT Health, the EU-backed health innovation community.

- Dates: 24–25 November 2026
- Place: Madrid (in person)
- Milestone: 10th anniversary of EIT Health
- Event page: https://www.eit.europa.eu/news-events/events/eit-health-summit-2026

Madrid is hosting the EIT Health Summit 2026 on 24 and 25 November, the first time the event has come to the city. The summit marks ten years of EIT Health, the health innovation community of the European Institute of Innovation and Technology. Sessions look at partnerships and the next decade of healthcare innovation in Europe.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Ullswater Investments analysis: EIT Health runs accelerators, innovation projects and funding calls for health startups and SMEs. Hosting the summit raises the visibility of the Spanish health innovation ecosystem among its European partners.

## Madrid's 2027 budget raises industrial aid to €44 million
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/madrid-2027-budget-industrial-aid-44-million/
Date: 2026-11-25 · Category: Spain · Source: Comunidad de Madrid (https://www.comunidad.madrid/noticias/2026/11/23/comunidad-madrid-presenta-empresarios-presupuestos-regionales-contemplan-recursos-industria-autonomos)

The regional draft budget increases industrial aid by 13%, equipment grants for small industrial firms to €19 million and digitalisation aid by 10%.

- Presented: To business leaders at CEIM, 23 November 2026
- Total 2027 budget: €32.911 billion (+7.3%)
- Industrial aid: €44 million (+13%)
- Equipment grants, small industrial firms: From €15 million to €19 million
- Digitalisation aid: +10%
- Training in biotech, AI and quantum: €27 million
- Status: Pending approval by the Madrid Assembly

The Community of Madrid has presented its draft 2027 budget to the business community. Industrial aid rises to €44 million, 13% more than this year. Grants for equipment in small industrial firms grow from €15 million to €19 million, and digitalisation aid increases by 10%.
The draft also earmarks more than €16 million for the 2026–2029 Family Business Support Strategy and €27 million for training in biotechnology, artificial intelligence and quantum computing. The total regional budget is €32.9 billion, up 7.3%. The regional parliament has yet to approve it.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Ullswater Investments analysis: the figures show which Madrid support lines will grow in 2027. Industrial SMEs planning equipment or digitalisation investments can expect larger calls next year.

## Cristina Oyón becomes the first woman to lead the Basque development agency SPRI
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/cristina-oyon-director-general-spri/
Date: 2026-11-25 · Category: Spain · Source: SPRI (https://www.spri.eus/es/blog/competitividad-industrial/cristina-oyon-nueva-directora-general-del-grupo-spri/)

The Basque Government appoints the head of SPRI's technology and innovation area, who will manage the Transformative Projects of the Euskadi 2030 Industry Plan.

- Appointed: Basque Government, 24 November 2026
- Replaces: Jon Ansoleaga
- Background: Head of SPRI's technology, innovation and sustainability area since 2020
- European roles: Vice-president of EURADA; former member of the Commission's "Industry 2030" high-level group
- Remit: Transformative Projects of the Euskadi 2030 Industry Plan

The Basque Government has appointed Cristina Oyón as director general of the SPRI Group, the Basque business development agency. She is the first woman to hold the post. She has led SPRI's technology, innovation and sustainability area since 2020 and is vice-president of EURADA, the European Association of Development Agencies.
Her mandate includes receiving and assessing the Transformative Projects under the Euskadi 2030 Industry Plan.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Ullswater Investments analysis: SPRI runs most Basque business support programmes, many of which are not published in Spain's national grants database, so changes in its leadership may shape the 2027 programmes.

## CDTI to act as secretariat of Spain's new commission on technology sovereignty
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/cdti-secretariat-cictiap-technology-sovereignty-commission/
Date: 2026-11-25 · Category: Spain · Source: CDTI (https://www.cdti.es/noticias/cdti-secretaria-nueva-comision-interministerial-cictiap-ciencia-tecnologia-innovacion-autonomia-proyectos-estrategicos)

Created by Royal Decree-law 40/2026, the CICTIAP commission will first assess up to 20 national interest centres and takes over Spain's Deep Tech Strategy.

- Legal basis: Royal Decree-law 40/2026 (Official State Gazette, 21 November 2026)
- Body: Interministerial Commission for Science, Technology and Innovation for Strategic Autonomy (CICTIAP), attached to the Ministry of Science
- Vice-presidencies: Digital Transformation, Economy, Defence and Industry
- Secretariat: CDTI
- First task: Assess the designation of up to 20 national interest centres
- Also: Takes over governance of the Deep Tech Strategy 2026–2030

CDTI will act as secretariat of CICTIAP, the new interministerial commission created by Royal Decree-law 40/2026 to steer science, technology and innovation policy towards strategic autonomy. The commission has four vice-presidencies, held by the ministries for Digital Transformation, Economy, Defence and Industry.
Its first task is to assess the designation of up to 20 national interest centres. It also takes over the functions of the committee in charge of Spain's Deep Tech Strategy 2026–2030.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Ullswater Investments analysis: CDTI's central role suggests that public funding for strategic technologies such as semiconductors, AI, quantum and space will be coordinated more closely across ministries.

## Castilla y León opens €5.4 million ERDF call for applied-science research
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/castilla-y-leon-erdf-applied-science-research-call/
Date: 2026-11-25 · Category: Spain · Source: BOCYL – Boletín Oficial de Castilla y León (https://bocyl.jcyl.es/boletines/2026/11/24/pdf/BOCYL-D-24112026-227-8.pdf)

The call funds applied-science research projects starting in 2027 at universities, public research bodies and health research foundations in the region.

- Published: BOCYL No. 227, 24 November 2026 (BDNS 943540)
- Budget: Up to €5.4 million, co-funded by the ERDF
- Scope: Applied-science research projects starting in 2027
- Eligible: Universities, public research organisations, ICTS and health research foundations based in Castilla y León
- Deadline: 21 December 2026

The regional government of Castilla y León has opened a €5.4 million call, co-funded by the European Regional Development Fund, for applied-science research projects starting in 2027. Universities, public research organisations, singular scientific and technical infrastructures and health research foundations based in the region can apply until 21 December 2026.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Ullswater Investments analysis: the call is not open to companies directly, but it funds research groups that often partner with industry, so it is a way to start collaborations with regional research centres.

## Basque project Q-CLINIC uses quantum-inspired AI to streamline clinical studies
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/basque-q-clinic-quantum-ai-clinical-studies/
Date: 2026-11-25 · Category: Health & Health Data · Source: SPRI (https://www.spri.eus/es/blog/teics-comunicacion/q-clinic-mejora-el-rendimiento-de-los-estudios-clinicos-gracias-a-la-inteligencia-artificial-cuantica/)

Led by Ubikare with Vicomtech and Multiverse Computing, the project is funded by SPRI's Smart Industry – Quantum Technologies 2025 programme.

- Funding: SPRI Smart Industry – Quantum Technologies 2025 (Basque Government)
- Consortium: Ubikare (lead), Vicomtech, Multiverse Computing
- What it does: Turns clinical notes into coded data (SNOMED CT, LOINC, HL7/FHIR)
- Duration: 16 months, until spring 2027
- Goal: Cut administrative workload by 30–40%

A Basque consortium led by Ubikare, with the research centre Vicomtech and the quantum software company Multiverse Computing, is developing Q-CLINIC. The project uses quantum-inspired AI to turn clinicians' free-text notes into structured data coded to international standards such as SNOMED CT, LOINC and HL7/FHIR.
The 16-month project is funded by SPRI's Smart Industry – Quantum Technologies 2025 programme and will run until spring 2027. Its goal is to cut the administrative workload of health professionals by 30–40%.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Ullswater Investments analysis: structured, interoperable health data is a precondition for the European Health Data Space. The project also shows how Basque programmes, which do not always appear in Spain's national grants database, fund applied quantum and AI work.

## Basque energy agency EVE invests in BiMEP marine energy test site
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/basque-eve-bimep-marine-energy-capital-increase/
Date: 2026-11-25 · Category: Climate & Energy · Source: BOPV – Boletín Oficial del País Vasco (https://www.euskadi.eus/web01-bopv/es/bopv2/datos/2026/11/2605025a.shtml)

EVE will put €487,500 into a €650,000 capital increase for the Biscay Marine Energy Platform, with Spain's IDAE covering the rest.

- Instrument: Decree 187/2026 (BOPV No. 225, 24 November 2026)
- Capital increase: €650,000
- EVE share: 75% (€487,500)
- IDAE share: 25% (€162,500)
- Purpose: BiMEP's planned investments (€633,000)
- Site: Armintza (Biscay)

The Basque Government has authorised its energy agency EVE to put €487,500 into a €650,000 capital increase for BiMEP, the Biscay Marine Energy Platform. Spain's IDAE covers the remaining 25%.
The money funds BiMEP's planned investments, which total €633,000, at its offshore test site for marine renewable energy converters in Armintza.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Ullswater Investments analysis: open-sea test sites like BiMEP are key infrastructure for marine energy companies that need to validate their technology before preparing EU-funded demonstration projects.

## Aragon awards €9 million in ERDF funding for municipal waste recycling
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/aragon-erdf-9-million-municipal-waste-recycling/
Date: 2026-11-25 · Category: Climate & Energy · Source: BOA – Boletín Oficial de Aragón (https://www.boa.aragon.es/cgi-bin/EBOA/BRSCGI?CMD=VEROBJ&MLKOB=1476468351212&type=pdf)

The call drew 59 applications worth €20.9 million; local authorities and waste consortia receive 75% of eligible costs.

- Instrument: Order MAT/1701/2026 (BOA No. 228, 25 November 2026)
- Programme: ERDF Aragon 2021–2027
- Budget: €9 million
- Demand: 59 applications requesting €20.87 million
- Lines: Composting plants, equipment, separate collection, recycling points, other equipment
- Aid: 75% of eligible costs
- Beneficiaries: Local authorities and waste consortia

Aragon has resolved a €9 million call under its ERDF 2021–2027 programme to boost preparation for reuse and recycling of municipal waste. The 59 applications requested €20.9 million, more than twice the available budget.
Local authorities and waste consortia will receive 75% of eligible costs for composting plants, separate collection, recycling points and equipment.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Ullswater Investments analysis: the resolution will lead to public tenders for waste equipment and infrastructure in Aragon, which are business opportunities for suppliers of circular-economy technology.

## Spain's State Research Agency opens €10 million call for R&D technical and management staff
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/aei-2026-call-rd-technical-management-staff-10-million/
Date: 2026-11-25 · Category: Spain · Source: Agencia Estatal de Investigación (AEI) (https://www.aei.gob.es/convocatorias/buscador-convocatorias/ayudas-contratos-personal-tecnico-gestion-idi-2026-0)

Research bodies, universities, health research institutes and technology centres can apply until 17 December for three-year contracts.

- Call: 2026 grants for R&D&I technical and management staff (AEI)
- Budget: Up to €10 million (€235,200 reserved for people with a disability of 33% or more)
- Deadlines: Candidates: 10 December; institutions: 17 December 2026, 14:00
- Eligible: Public research bodies, universities, National Health System bodies, accredited health research institutes, State technology centres, other non-profit R&D centres
- Aid: €19,600/year (graduates) or €16,300/year (higher technicians), for 3 years

Spain's State Research Agency has opened its 2026 call to fund contracts for technical and R&D&I management staff, with a budget of up to €10 million. Research bodies, universities, health research institutes, technology centres and other non-profit R&D centres can apply.
Candidates must register by 10 December and institutions must submit applications by 17 December 2026 at 14:00. The grant covers three-year contracts at €19,600 per year for graduates or €16,300 per year for higher technicians.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Ullswater Investments analysis: project management and technical support staff are a frequent bottleneck when research centres prepare and run Horizon Europe projects. This call helps them strengthen those teams.

## Red NEURONA starts in Extremadura with 28 interested companies
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/red-neurona-launches-extremadura-pilot-28-companies/
Date: 2026-11-23 · Category: Spain · Source: Europa Press (via Onda Cero Extremadura) (https://ondacerosur.es/2026/11/el-gobierno-inicia-en-extremadura-la-red-neurona-para-acercar-la-inteligencia-artificial-a-las-pequenas-empresas/)

First Vice-President Carlos Cuerpo opened Plan IA360's network of AI demonstration centres in Olivenza; CDTI and ICEX will mentor the companies.

- Date: 23 November 2026
- Place: Olivenza (Badajoz), Extremadura
- Presided by: Carlos Cuerpo, First Vice-President of the Government
- Companies: 28 Extremadura companies interested in the pilot
- Support: Mentoring through CDTI and ICEX; CDTI and ICO financing discussed
- Next step: Extension to more autonomous communities during 2027

The Government held the constitutive session of Red NEURONA, the public-private and territorial network of AI demonstration and deployment centres in Plan IA360, in Olivenza (Badajoz). It was chaired by First Vice-President Carlos Cuerpo and attended by 28 Extremadura companies interested in the model.
The companies will be mentored through CDTI and ICEX to identify the best technology options for their problems. Financing from CDTI and ICO was put on the table, along with a possible subsidy to lower project costs, and an advanced capacity centre will be set up to help develop projects and prototypes.
The Government plans to extend the project to more autonomous communities during 2027.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Ullswater Investments analysis: this is the first visible step of the NEURONA roll-out. Amounts and access rules have not been published, so interested SMEs and technology providers in other regions should follow which communities join next and how CDTI and ICO financing will be channelled.

## Ullswater launches its Funding Assistant, an AI chat for EU calls and Spanish grants
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/ullswater-launches-ai-funding-assistant/
Date: 2026-11-22 · Category: Spain · Source: Ullswater Investments (https://www.ullswaterinvestments.com/)

The free assistant, now on every Ullswater website, answers questions on 465 open and forthcoming EU calls, more than 150 Spanish State and regional grants, funding news and events, and links each answer to its source.

- What it is: A free AI chat assistant ("Asistente de ayudas" in Spanish) on every Ullswater Investments website
- What it covers: 465 open and forthcoming EU calls, Spanish State and regional grants for companies, EU funding news, events and webinars, and Ullswater's services and European projects
- Languages: English and Spanish
- How it works: Claude (Anthropic) searching the data published on Ullswater's websites, updated every day; every answer links to the call, grant or page it comes from
- Talk to an expert: One-hour Teams meetings, Monday to Friday, 10:00–11:00 (Madrid time)
- Privacy: No registration; questions are stored anonymously for 12 months, without IP addresses

Ullswater Investments has launched its Funding Assistant, a free AI chat available on all its websites: www.ullswaterinvestments.com, the EU calls site calls.ullswaterinvestments.com, this news site, the events site and the sites of the European R&D projects Ullswater takes part in. The assistant opens from the button at the bottom right of every page and works in English and Spanish.
The assistant answers questions in plain language. It can find, filter and compare the 465 open and forthcoming EU calls published on calls.ullswaterinvestments.com, read the official topic text to explain what a call funds and who can apply, and list the open Spanish State and regional grants for companies taken from the official BDNS database, filtered by region and company size. It also searches the news and events published by Ullswater, including info days, brokerage events and the Commission webinars library, and explains Ullswater's services and its European projects that are open to new partners.
Every specific fact comes from the data published on Ullswater's websites, which are updated every day from the EU Funding & Tenders Portal, the Spanish BDNS and official sources, and each answer links to the call, grant or page it is based on. The assistant knows the page the user is reading, so a reader of a news article or a call page can simply ask what it means for their organisation. It is built on Claude, Anthropic's AI model, and states clearly that users are talking to an AI system.
When a user needs help to apply, find partners or prepare a proposal, the assistant offers a one-hour Teams meeting with an Ullswater expert, bookable online from Monday to Friday between 10:00 and 11:00 (Madrid time). No registration is needed to use the chat: questions are stored anonymously for 12 months to improve the service, without IP addresses, as explained in Ullswater's privacy policy.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Ullswater Investments analysis: public funding information is scattered across the EU Funding & Tenders Portal, the Spanish BDNS and dozens of regional agencies, and it is written in programme language. The assistant puts EU calls and Spanish grants behind a single question, in English or Spanish, so companies, universities and research centres can check in minutes whether there is funding for their project before deciding whether to apply.

## Spain selects bodies for five EU4Health joint actions: 5-day window
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/spain-eu4health-2026-joint-actions-selection/
Date: 2026-11-21 · Category: Health & Health Data · Source: Boletín Oficial del Estado (BOE) · Orden SND/1258/2026 (https://www.boe.es/diario_boe/txt.php?id=BOE-A-2026-24491)

The Spanish Ministry of Health opens a competitive procedure to nominate the Spanish entities that will join five EU4Health joint actions under the 2026 Work Plan.

- Legal basis: Orden SND/1258/2026, of 12 November (BOE no. 290, 21 November 2026)
- Programme: EU4Health, 2026 Work Plan, managed by HaDEA
- Joint actions: Five: EU4H-2027-JA-HERA-IBA-01 and -02, EU4H-2027-JA-SANTE-IBA-01, -02 and -03
- EU co-funding per action: €5,000,000 · €15,000,000 · €24,850,000 · €7,900,000 · €3,330,000
- Who can apply: Public-sector legal entities and supervised non-profit entities whose activity includes health research and innovation, tax-resident in Spain
- Deadline: Five working days from the day after publication in the BOE

Spain's Ministry of Health has published an order that sets the competitive procedure for choosing which Spanish authorities and bodies will take part, with funding as beneficiaries, in the joint actions approved in the 2026 Work Plan of the EU4Health programme. Joint actions are carried out with Member States' authorities, and the EU regulation does not set how each country picks its participants, so the ministry is doing it through a published call.
Five joint actions are open. Two come from DG HERA: coordinating whole genome sequencing activities for preparedness and response (€5 million of EU co-funding) and strengthening EU deployable diagnostic capacities and pre-positioned medical countermeasures (€15 million). Three come from DG SANTE: enhancing public health security in the Union (€24.85 million), capacity building and AI capabilities in the European medicines regulatory network (€7.9 million), and reinforced market surveillance of medical devices and in vitro diagnostics, JAMS 3.0 (€3.33 million).
Only public-sector legal entities and non-profit entities supervised by the competent authorities, whose activity includes health research and innovation and that are tax-resident in Spain, can apply. Applications go by email to the ministry unit responsible for each action, using the forms annexed to the order, within five working days from the day after publication. Each unit proposes its candidates, the Secretary of State for Health resolves, and HaDEA then continues the grant procedure with the nominated authorities.
The assessment is a pass/fail check against criteria such as legal competence in the field, capacity to coordinate consortia, quality and European added value of the proposal, alignment with the ministry's priorities, and previous experience in joint actions and European projects.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Ullswater Investments analysis: joint actions are one of the few EU4Health routes that only Member State authorities can enter, and the national nomination is the gate. The window is very short, so eligible hospitals, research institutes and agencies should already have a clear idea of their role, their affiliated entities and their own co-funding before writing to the ministry. Experience in previous joint actions and European projects weighs in the assessment, so a short, evidence-based track record is worth preparing. Private companies cannot apply directly, but they may later work with nominated bodies within the rules of each action.

## STEP report: almost €24 billion mobilised and 614 Seals awarded
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/step-report-24-billion-614-projects/
Date: 2026-11-19 · Category: EU Budget & Policy · Source: European Commission – Press corner (IP/26/2356) (https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/ip_26_2356)

The second annual STEP report shows €23.9 billion of EU funds mobilised by end-2025, €5.3 billion in direct calls last year and defence added as a fourth sector.

- EU funds mobilised (end-2025): €23.9 billion: €10 billion direct management, €13.9 billion cohesion
- STEP Seals: 614 in total, 452 of them in 2025
- Direct STEP calls in 2025: €5.3 billion (€3.5 billion clean tech, €746 million digital, €509 million biotech, €553 million multi-sector)
- Sectors: Digital, clean tech, biotech and, since 2025, defence
- Cumulative EU contribution: €30 billion (€15 billion direct, €15 billion cohesion)

The European Commission has published the second annual report on the Strategic Technologies for Europe Platform (STEP), covering 2025. STEP, in place since March 2024, steers existing EU programmes towards critical technologies. By the end of 2025 it had mobilised €23.9 billion of EU funds: €10 billion through programmes managed directly by the Commission and €13.9 billion reprogrammed from cohesion policy funds.
In 2025 the Defence Readiness Omnibus added defence as a fourth STEP sector next to digital, clean tech and biotech. As a result, Digital Europe and the EIC Accelerator can now fund dual-use technologies, and the EIC's STEP Scale Up call is also open to defence-only projects. Directly managed STEP calls totalled €5.3 billion in 2025: €3.5 billion for clean tech, €746 million for digital, €509 million for biotech and €553 million for multi-sector calls. A total of 614 STEP Seals have been awarded, 452 of them in 2025, and more than 200 sealed projects appear on a Dealroom dashboard aimed at investors.
On the cohesion side, by the end of 2025 19 countries had aligned funds with STEP through 96 programme amendments, and 54 calls had been launched in 11 countries. Eleven Member States had already selected projects, supporting an estimated 11,900 companies and 21,644 jobs. Spain is among the largest contributors, together with Germany, Italy and Romania. The cumulative EU contribution to STEP priorities now reaches €30 billion, split equally between direct management and cohesion.
The Commission says the STEP experience is feeding into its proposal for a European Competitiveness Fund for 2028-2034, which would bring together 14 programmes, and that the STEP Portal serves as a testbed for a future single access point to EU funding.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Ullswater Investments analysis: STEP is not a separate budget but a label that redirects money from existing programmes, so applicants should look for STEP-flagged topics in Horizon Europe, the EIC, Digital Europe and the Innovation Fund, and for STEP calls in their regional cohesion programmes. A STEP Seal is worth pursuing even when a proposal is not funded, because it helps when approaching national, regional and private funders. Spanish companies should check the STEP calls run by their regional and national managing authorities, since Spain is one of the main contributors on the cohesion side. Defence and dual-use firms gain new routes through the EIC and Digital Europe. The report also previews how the European Competitiveness Fund could work after 2027.

## EIB Group approves €14 billion, a third for EU energy autonomy
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/eib-group-approves-14-billion-energy-autonomy/
Date: 2026-11-19 · Category: Climate & Energy · Source: European Investment Bank (https://www.eib.org/en/press/all/2026-424-eib-group-approves-eur14-billion-in-new-financing-with-focus-on-eu-energy-autonomy)

The EIB and EIF Boards back €14 billion in new financing, with €4.2 billion for clean-energy infrastructure and €3.8 billion for business competitiveness.

- Total approved: €14 billion in new financing (EIB and EIF Boards, Luxembourg)
- Clean-energy infrastructure in the EU: €4.2 billion
- Business competitiveness: €3.8 billion, mainly through innovation
- Energy share: Around a third of the package

The Boards of Directors of the European Investment Bank and the European Investment Fund, meeting in Luxembourg this week, endorsed €14 billion in fresh financing. Energy accounts for around a third of the package, which the EIB Group presents as part of its effort to strengthen the EU's energy autonomy.
Within the EU, €4.2 billion goes to clean-energy infrastructure: district heating and cooling in Austria and Germany, renewable energy in France, Italy, Spain and Lithuania, and electricity grids in Cyprus and Hungary. A further €3.8 billion is earmarked for business competitiveness across Europe, mainly through support for innovation. Other approved projects cover water infrastructure in Belgium, schools in France, affordable housing in Ireland and urban development in Romania.
Outside the EU, the Boards backed waste management and plastics projects in Gabon, water infrastructure and climate resilience in Jordan, and climate adaptation and rural development in Uzbekistan, in line with the Global Gateway strategy. The Boards also endorsed revised codes of conduct covering conflicts of interest and cooling-off periods, which still need final approval by the EIB Board of Governors and the EIF General Meeting. In 2025 the EIB Group signed €100 billion in new financing and advisory services for over 870 projects.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Ullswater Investments analysis: these are Board approvals, not open calls, so companies cannot apply to this package directly. For energy and cleantech developers, the message is that the EIB Group keeps energy security and grids at the top of its lending, which matters when planning the debt side of projects that also seek EU grants such as the Innovation Fund. Innovative companies should note the share aimed at business competitiveness, which typically reaches them through direct EIB venture debt or through intermediated EIF products offered by local banks and funds. Spanish promoters of renewable projects should watch for the signature announcements that follow these approvals.

## EDF project D-STORM opens €90,000 cascade call for SMEs
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/edf-d-storm-cascade-funding-call-smes/
Date: 2026-11-18 · Category: EIC, Defence & Equity · Source: European Commission – Defence Industry and Space (https://defence-industry-space.ec.europa.eu/edf-d-storm-project-launches-first-open-call-cascade-funding-2026-11-18_en)

The European Defence Fund project D-STORM offers up to €10,000 to SMEs and start-ups with operational know-how on loitering munitions and combat drones, until 11 January 2027.

- Programme: European Defence Fund (EDF) – cascade funding
- Budget: €90,000 in total, up to €10,000 per recipient
- Who can apply: SMEs and start-ups in EU Member States, Norway or Ukraine
- Deadline: 11 January 2027, 11:00 CET

D-STORM (Drone-based Scalable Tactical Operations Responsive Munitions), a project funded by the European Defence Fund, launched its first open call for cascade funding on 18 November 2026, as announced by the Commission's Directorate-General for Defence Industry and Space. The project is developing affordable, scalable tactical munitions and the operational concepts that go with them.
The call looks for first-hand operational knowledge on loitering munitions and unmanned combat air systems to refine the project's concepts of operations and operational requirements. Relevant expertise includes swarm characteristics, the number and reusability of effectors, field constraints such as jamming, mission types, logistics and maintenance, pre-launch preparation, assembly and configuration of effectors, and their recovery.
Selected recipients will receive up to €10,000 each, from a total budget of €90,000. The call targets SMEs, including start-ups, established in EU Member States, Norway or Ukraine, with priority for entities operating directly in Ukraine. Over a period of up to four weeks, recipients will provide structured recommendations using the project's templates, take part in interviews with the technical teams and attend a workshop that may be held in Ukraine, for example in Kyiv or Lviv, or in an EU country. Applications are open until 11 January 2027 at 11:00 CET.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Ullswater Investments analysis: the amounts are small, but cascade calls like this one are a low-barrier way for SMEs with real field experience to work inside an EDF consortium, build references with defence primes and understand how EDF projects define their requirements. For companies considering future EDF or EDIP proposals, this kind of participation can be a useful first step. Applicants should document their operational experience precisely, since the call rewards first-hand knowledge rather than technology development.

## Innovation Fund 2026: €5.2 billion in five calls opening 3 December
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/innovation-fund-2026-calls-5-2-billion-info-days/
Date: 2026-11-17 · Category: Climate & Energy · Source: CINEA – European Climate, Infrastructure and Environment Executive Agency (https://cinea.ec.europa.eu/news-events/news/registrations-open-innovation-fund-2026-info-days-2026-11-17_en)

The Commission will launch three grant calls and two auctions under the Innovation Fund on 3 December, with online info days on 9, 10 and 15 December.

- Programme: Innovation Fund (IF26), funded by EU ETS revenues
- Total budget: Up to €5.2 billion across five calls
- Launch: 3 December: three grant calls and two auction calls
- Largest call: Net-Zero Technologies: €3.3 billion
- Info days: 9, 10 and 15 December 2026, online with live Q&A

The European Climate, Infrastructure and Environment Executive Agency (CINEA) announced on 17 November 2026 that the Commission plans to open five Innovation Fund calls on 3 December, with a combined budget of up to €5.2 billion. The package comprises three grant calls and two auction calls. Ahead of the launch, DG CLIMA and CINEA have opened registrations for four online info days, which will be livestreamed with a live Q&A.
The two auctions come first. The IF26 Hydrogen Auction, worth €500 million and aimed at renewable and electrolytic low-carbon hydrogen production, will be presented on 9 December from 09:30 to 13:00 CET. The IF26 Heat Auction, with €1 billion for process heat from electrified technologies, direct renewable heat and waste heat sources, follows the same day from 14:30 to 17:30 CET.
The IF26 SME Call, with €200 million, will be presented on 10 December from 09:30 to 13:00 CET. It will have two cut-off dates, at the end of March 2027 and at the end of September 2027, and CINEA may hold online orientation dialogues in December on request. Finally, on 15 December from 09:00 to 13:00 CET, the info day will cover the Net-Zero Technologies call, with €3.3 billion, and the Maritime call, with €200 million.
The full call conditions and application requirements will be published on the EU Funding and Tenders Portal. The Innovation Fund is financed by revenues from the EU Emissions Trading System and has so far committed over €18 billion to around 380 projects.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Ullswater Investments analysis: with the calls opening only a few weeks before the end of the year, project promoters should use the info days to confirm eligibility and the specific rules of each call rather than wait for the full documents. Auctions and grant calls follow different logics: auctions reward the lowest support requested per unit of output, while grant calls assess the project as a whole, so the choice of instrument shapes the whole preparation. The SME call, with two cut-off dates spread over 2027, gives smaller companies a more manageable route and time to mature a proposal before submitting.

## Horizon Europe opens €297 million digital calls with 12 topics
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/horizon-europe-digital-calls-297-million-ai/
Date: 2026-11-17 · Category: Digital & AI · Source: European Commission – Shaping Europe's digital future (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/commission-launches-over-eu290-million-boost-eu-tech-sovereignty-and-beyond)

Two new Horizon Europe calls under the digital strand cover frontier AI, AI-driven robotics, energy-efficient AI data centres and virtual worlds, open until 18 March 2027.

- Programme: Horizon Europe – Digital, Industry and Space (Work Programme 2026-27)
- Budget: €297 million across two calls and 12 topics
- AI topics: Four topics worth €107 million
- Data and AI services: Three topics worth €112 million
- Deadline: 18 March 2027

On 17 November 2026 the European Commission opened two new calls under the digital strand of Horizon Europe, bringing together 12 topics with a combined budget of €297 million. The calls belong to the Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026-27 for Digital, Industry and Space and will stay open until 18 March 2027.
The largest share goes to open strategic autonomy in digital and enabling technologies. Four AI topics, worth €107 million in total, address frontier AI that is safe by design, AI-driven robotics for industry, faster uptake of AI in key sectors and European AI solutions for low- and middle-income countries. Two further topics, totalling €29 million, cover advanced photonics and a European forum on emerging technologies.
A second block of three topics, worth €112 million, targets distributed, decentralised and energy-efficient AI processing, pilots on the Connected, Collaborative, Computing (3C) infrastructure driven by industry demand, and more sustainable, energy-efficient AI data centres. The final block, worth €49 million, funds hardware components for virtual worlds, a virtual worlds and Web 4.0 ecosystem, and European participation in international digital standardisation.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Ullswater Investments analysis: these topics mix research actions, innovation actions and coordination actions, so consortia should first check the action type of the topic they target, because it determines the expected maturity of the results and the funding rate. Several topics are linked to European partnerships in AI, photonics and virtual worlds, which makes it worth aligning proposals with those partnerships' agendas. With a single deadline in March, the window to build industry-led consortia, especially for the innovation actions on robotics, edge cloud and data centres, is short and should start now.

## EIC Fund survey: 64% say it was essential to close their round
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/eic-fund-survey-64-percent-essential-investment-round/
Date: 2026-11-17 · Category: EIC, Defence & Equity · Source: European Innovation Council (https://eic.ec.europa.eu/news/eic-fund-companies-highlight-its-role-supporting-fundraising-and-growth-2026-11-17_en)

A survey of 182 companies backed by the EIC Fund finds strong support for its role in fundraising, while asking for faster processes and more follow-on capacity.

- Respondents: 182 companies assigned to the EIC Fund in 2019–2025 (24% of 752 invited)
- Essential to the round: 64% of companies with signed investment agreements
- Grant plus equity: 72% see the combination as complementary
- Recommendation score: 8.6 out of 10
- Dual use and defence: Relevant to 45% of respondents

The European Innovation Council and SMEs Executive Agency (EISMEA) published on 17 November 2026 the results of a survey of companies supported by the EIC Fund, the EIC's equity arm for start-ups and SMEs. The survey was launched in March 2026 and collected answers from 182 companies assigned to the Fund between 2019 and 2025, which represents 24% of the 752 companies invited to take part.
Among companies that had signed investment agreements, 64% said the EIC Fund had been essential to completing their investment round, and another 17% reported a positive impact. In total, 72% of respondents considered the mix of EIC grant and equity support complementary, and companies gave an average score of 8.6 out of 10 when asked how likely they were to recommend applying to the EIC. Among companies selected since 2023, 58% said the effect on the timing of their fundraising was positive or neutral.
The survey also shows that dual-use and defence-related activities are relevant to 45% of the responding companies. At the same time, respondents identified areas where the Fund could do better: more capacity for follow-on investments, faster processes, lighter administrative requirements and clearer communication of investment decisions. EISMEA says the findings will be used to further improve the EIC Fund and its investment processes.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Ullswater Investments analysis: for deep tech companies weighing an EIC Accelerator application, the equity component is often what convinces co-investors to commit, so it deserves as much attention in the proposal as the grant. The feedback on timing and administrative load is a reminder to plan the fundraising calendar with margin and to have due diligence documentation ready early. The weight of dual-use activities among respondents also confirms that companies with defence-relevant technologies can find a natural place in the EIC portfolio.

## AI Office seeks up to 100 European AI providers for SMEs via EDIHs
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/ai-office-call-european-ai-providers-edih-sme/
Date: 2026-11-17 · Category: Digital & AI · Source: European Commission – Shaping Europe's digital future (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/call-expression-interest-european-ai-providers)

European AI providers with market-ready solutions can apply until 17 December 2026 to join an 'EDIH Ready' catalogue that Digital Innovation Hubs will offer to SMEs.

- Initiative: Call for expression of interest under the Apply AI Strategy
- Places: Up to 100 AI providers in the first edition
- Deadline: 17 December 2026, 17:00 CET (may close earlier)
- Eligibility: Mature AI solutions; providers headquartered in the EU or Digital Europe associated countries

The European Commission's AI Office opened on 17 November 2026 a call for expression of interest for European AI providers that want to present mature AI solutions to the network of European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs). The goal, set out in the Apply AI Strategy, is to bridge supply and demand by helping SMEs across Europe adopt European AI, with EDIHs acting as trusted intermediaries. The hubs have already delivered services to more than 50,000 organisations.
The first edition is open to up to 100 providers. Solutions must be ready for deployment in SMEs: proofs of concept, research projects, minimum viable products and solutions not yet on the market are not suitable. Eligibility depends on where the provider is headquartered, which must be an EU Member State or a country associated to the Digital Europe Programme. Submissions are made in English through an EU Survey form by 17 December 2026 at 17:00 CET, and the call may close earlier if 100 suitable solutions arrive first.
Selected solutions will form a catalogue on the AI-on-Demand Platform, listed in the Business Navigator with an 'EDIH Ready' label. Details of suitable candidates will be shared with DeployAI, the EU-funded consortium behind the platform, which will handle onboarding, and information sessions with EDIHs are planned for the first quarter of 2027.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Ullswater Investments analysis: this is not a grant, but it gives European AI companies a direct channel to SME customers through a network the Commission funds, which can shorten sales cycles and add credibility. Because places are limited and the call can close early, providers with a product already deployed at customers should apply soon and present clear evidence of market readiness. Visibility in the catalogue may also help when preparing proposals for future Digital Europe or Horizon Europe uptake actions that involve EDIHs.

## EIC Accelerator picks 35 deep tech firms for €84 million in grants
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/eic-accelerator-35-companies-84-million/
Date: 2026-11-16 · Category: EIC, Defence & Equity · Source: European Innovation Council (https://eic.ec.europa.eu/news/european-innovation-council-selects-35-deep-tech-companies-its-accelerator-support-2026-11-16_en)

Out of 453 full applications, 35 start-ups and SMEs from 17 countries were selected; 32 of them will be assessed for EIC Fund equity of up to €10 million each.

- Selected companies: 35 start-ups and SMEs from 17 EU and associated countries
- Competition: 453 full applications, 88 interviewed
- Grant funding: €84 million in total proposed grants
- Equity: 32 companies to be assessed for EIC Fund investments of up to €10 million each
- Seals: 74 Seals of Excellence and 13 STEP Seals

The European Innovation Council announced on 16 November 2026 the results of its latest EIC Accelerator evaluation round, linked to the May–July 2026 cut-off. Of the 453 companies that submitted full applications, 88 were invited to interview and 35 start-ups and SMEs were finally selected. The total proposed grant funding for them is €84 million, and the large majority (32 companies) will also be assessed by the EIC Fund for equity investments of up to €10 million each.
The selected companies come from 17 EU and associated countries, with France, Switzerland and Germany contributing the most. Women hold key leadership roles such as CEO, CTO or CSO in 31% of them. Examples highlighted by the EIC include autonomous underwater robots for seabed mapping (DEESS, France), biorefineries that turn coffee waste into ingredients (Ecobean, Poland), light-based destruction of PFAS (Oxyle, Switzerland), desalination with mineral recovery from brine (Seamoretech, Portugal) and microbiome-enabled organ-on-chip technology (Sia Cellboxlab, Latvia).
A further 74 applications scored above the threshold but could not be funded and will receive a Seal of Excellence, while 13 companies that met the criteria under the five EIC Accelerator challenges will receive a STEP Seal. Both seals can help them access other EU funding. Grant agreements are expected to be finalised within the next three months, and the EIC Fund will decide on equity investments, co-investing with other private and public investors.
As a reminder, the EIC Accelerator offers grants of up to €2.5 million and EIC Fund equity between €1 million and €10 million, with up to €30 million in equity under EIC STEP Scale-up. Applications can be submitted at any time: short proposals are batched monthly and assessed within 4 to 6 weeks, while full proposals are batched four times per year.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Ullswater Investments analysis: with only a small share of full applications funded, the EIC Accelerator remains one of the most selective instruments in Horizon Europe, and the interview stage is where most projects are decided. Companies that scored above the threshold should not treat the Seal of Excellence or STEP Seal as a dead end: they can open doors to national and regional funding, and a well-documented resubmission often performs better. For deep tech start-ups preparing for 2027, the continuous short-proposal route is the best way to test eligibility early and plan a full application around a realistic cut-off.

## EHDS webinar on 25 November: benefits of health data secondary use
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/ehds-webinar-4-secondary-use-health-data/
Date: 2026-11-16 · Category: Health & Health Data · Source: European Commission · EHDS support to stakeholders (official event page) (https://events.teams.microsoft.com/event/a9526537-8a2b-448d-9045-59470ebf0b13@b853f977-4183-428f-855c-ffe7328b6f13)

The fourth webinar of the Commission's EHDS stakeholder support series discusses the benefits, challenges and incentives of reusing health data. Open to all.

- Event: EHDS support to stakeholders · Webinar 4: Stakeholder workshop on Benefits, challenges and incentives of EHDS secondary use
- Date: Wednesday 25 November 2026, 11:00–12:30 CET
- Format: Online (Microsoft Teams), open to anyone after registration
- Moderators: Verena Thaler, Yann Heyer (European Patients' Forum), Valentina Colcelli (CNR-IFAC) and Sarah Collen
- Framework: European Health Data Space Regulation (EU) 2025/327

The European Commission's EHDS stakeholder support series holds its fourth webinar on Wednesday 25 November 2026, from 11:00 to 12:30 CET. The online workshop is dedicated to the secondary use of health data under the European Health Data Space: how it can create value through more efficient, transparent and trustworthy access to health data, and which benefits matter most to each group of stakeholders.
Four moderators lead the discussion: Verena Thaler, a senior expert in digital health and EHDS data governance; Yann Heyer, senior policy officer at the European Patients' Forum; Valentina Colcelli, senior researcher at Italy's National Research Council (CNR-IFAC), who works on the governance of health research data; and Sarah Collen, an EU policy manager working on the EHDS, cancer policy and data protection.
The session is open: anyone can watch and take part after registering on the official event page on Microsoft Teams. Ullswater Investments has published the full event details, moderators and official links in English and Spanish on EU Funding Events.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Ullswater Investments analysis: the secondary use rules of the EHDS will shape how researchers, companies and public bodies can access health data across Europe, and data holders will carry new obligations. Understanding the benefits and incentives that each stakeholder group expects is useful for anyone building a health data space, offering services to data holders or preparing an EU proposal that relies on reusing health data. It is a good opportunity to hear patients, researchers and clinicians on the same panel before the implementing rules are finalised.

## EU launches first global alliance of climate and health funders
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/global-climate-health-research-funders-alliance/
Date: 2026-11-13 · Category: Health & Health Data · Source: European Commission – Research and Innovation (https://research-and-innovation.ec.europa.eu/news/all-research-and-innovation-news/commission-launches-first-global-alliance-climate-and-health-research-funding-cop31-2026-11-13_en)

Launched at COP 31 with the Wellcome Trust, the initiative will align research funders' priorities. A secretariat starts work in January 2027.

- Initiative: Multilateral Initiative on Climate & Health Research Funding
- Founding support: European Commission and Wellcome Trust, with nine national public funders
- Secretariat: From January 2027, hosted by ANR, ZonMw, IDRC and UEFISCDI
- EU funding: Coordination and Support Action grant running until December 2029

The European Commission used COP 31 to launch the Multilateral Initiative on Climate & Health Research Funding, together with the Wellcome Trust and public research funders from five continents. The Commission presents it as the first global alliance of funders focused on how climate change affects health. Its aim is to help funders coordinate their investment and research priorities, cut fragmentation and move results faster into policy, technology and practice.
Throughout 2026 the initiative has been shaped by a Design Group made up of the Commission, the Wellcome Trust and nine national funders: NHMRC (Australia), IDRC (Canada), ANR (France), ZonMw (Netherlands), the Philippines Department of Health, UEFISCDI (Romania), SAMRC (South Africa), TSRI (Thailand) and UKRI (United Kingdom), in consultation with the World Health Organization and the wider research community.
The alliance has five strategic goals, ranging from building a stronger global research community and making better use of funding to clearer pathways to impact. Once launched, membership will be open to any organisation that funds climate and health research. From January 2027 a permanent secretariat will be hosted by four Design Group members (ANR, ZonMw, IDRC and UEFISCDI), funded by a European Commission Coordination and Support Action grant running until December 2029.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Ullswater Investments analysis: the alliance does not open a call, but it signals where funders intend to put coordinated effort. Climate and health research is likely to gain visibility in national and EU work programmes, and alignment between funders can lead to joint or complementary calls over time. Research teams and companies working on heat, infectious disease, air quality or health-system resilience should follow the initiative's work and frame their proposals around these shared priorities.

---

## ERC Synergy Grants 2026: €500 million for 48 research teams
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/erc-synergy-grants-2026-500-million-48-teams/
Date: 2026-11-12 · Category: Research Policy · Source: European Research Council (https://erc.europa.eu/news-events/news/erc-2026-synergy-grants-results)

The European Research Council selected 48 teams out of 957 proposals, a record number of applications, for frontier research projects worth €10.4 million on average.

- Programme: ERC Synergy Grants, Horizon Europe
- Budget: €500 million in total
- Teams funded: 48 (957 proposals submitted)
- Average grant: €10.4 million per project
- Success rate: About one in twenty proposals
- Host countries: 26 countries; most projects in the UK (23), Germany (22), France (14) and the US (12)

The European Research Council (ERC) announced on 12 November 2026 the results of its 2026 Synergy Grants call: 48 research teams will share a total of €500 million, an average of €10.4 million per project. The grants are part of Horizon Europe and fund groups of two to four researchers who combine complementary expertise to tackle ambitious scientific questions.
The call received 957 proposals, the highest number since Synergy Grants were launched in 2012, and about one in twenty was selected. The funded teams are based at universities and research centres in 26 countries in Europe and beyond. The United Kingdom hosts researchers in 23 projects, Germany in 22, France in 14 and the United States in 12.
Around 35% of the funded projects involve researchers based outside the EU and associated countries, mostly in the United States; Commissioner Ekaterina Zaharieva noted that 17 of the 48 teams include researchers based outside Europe. Women account for about 25% of the researchers in the selected projects, while they were 33% of the 3,312 principal investigators named in the submitted proposals.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Ullswater Investments analysis: with roughly a 5% success rate, Synergy Grants reward teams whose combined expertise is clearly greater than the sum of their parts, so the case for why these specific researchers must work together carries as much weight as the scientific idea. Research centres and universities thinking of applying should build that argument early, starting from a question no single group could answer alone. The strong presence of researchers outside Europe also shows that the scheme is open to international teams.

## CDTI opens €150 million INNTERCONECTA-STEP call on 17 November
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/cdti-innterconecta-step-2026-150-million/
Date: 2026-11-12 · Category: Spain · Source: Boletín Oficial del Estado (BOE) – CDTI call extract (https://www.boe.es/diario_boe/txt.php?id=BOE-B-2026-37016)

Spain's regional R&D consortia call funds company-led projects in STEP technologies, with at least €10 million reserved for women's health.

- Programme: Consorcios Regionales INNTERCONECTA-STEP 2026 (CDTI, co-financed by ERDF 2021-2027)
- Budget: €150 million maximum; at least €10 million reserved for women's health
- Applications: 17 November to 23 December 2026, 12:00 (peninsular time)
- Project size: €1 million to €4 million eligible budget; at least €175,000 per company
- Consortia: 2 to 6 companies, including at least one SME
- Duration: Start 1 January 2027; end 31 December 2028 or 30 June 2029

Spain's Official State Gazette (BOE) published on 12 November the extract of the 2026 INNTERCONECTA-STEP call, approved by the presidency of CDTI on 6 November. The call supports cooperative R&D projects led by companies in the strategic technology fields of the EU's STEP platform: digital technologies, clean and resource-efficient technologies, and biotechnologies. It has a maximum budget of €150 million and is co-financed by the European Regional Development Fund (ERDF) 2021-2027.
This edition sets aside at least €10 million for proposals addressing women's health, specifically conditions with a greater impact on women. If there are not enough fundable proposals in that strand, the unused amount can be allocated to other eligible projects according to their ranking.
Applicants must form groups of two to six companies, at least two of them independent from each other and at least one an SME. No company, or set of linked companies, may hold more than 70% of the eligible budget, and each entity may appear in no more than two applications. The group has no legal personality, so one member acts as coordinator, and the partners must sign an internal agreement before applying. At least 10% of the eligible budget must be subcontracted to research organisations.
The work must take place in at least two of these regions: Andalucía, Illes Balears, Canarias, Castilla-La Mancha, Castilla y León, Comunidad Valenciana, Extremadura, Galicia and Región de Murcia. Projects are multi-year, with an eligible budget between €1 million and €4 million, a minimum of €175,000 per company, and a start date of 1 January 2027. Applications open on 17 November and close on 23 December 2026 at noon, peninsular time.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): With a short window between opening and closing, and a consortium agreement required before submission, the real constraint is partner building, not writing. Consortia need companies active in at least two of the eligible regions plus a research organisation ready to take a meaningful subcontract, so groups that already work together have a clear head start. The women's health reserve is worth a close look for medtech, biotech and digital health firms: a ring-fenced amount can mean less competition than in the general pool. Companies should also watch the limit of two applications per entity and the 70% ceiling per partner when deciding which consortia to join and how to split the budget.

## Australia signs deal to join Horizon Europe's Pillar II
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/australia-signs-horizon-europe-association/
Date: 2026-11-12 · Category: Research Policy · Source: European Commission – Press release (https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/ip_26_2418)

Australian organisations will be able to join and lead Pillar II consortia, with transitional access to calls from January 2027.

- Scope: Horizon Europe Pillar II, worth €52.4 billion
- Signed: In Brussels, by Commissioner Ekaterina Zaharieva and Minister Tim Ayres
- Transitional access: From January 2027 for Pillar II calls
- Formal completion: Expected by mid-2027, after Australian parliamentary scrutiny
- Associated countries: Australia becomes the 24th

The EU and Australia have signed an agreement that associates Australia to Pillar II of Horizon Europe, the part of the programme that funds collaborative research in fields such as health, climate, energy and digital technologies. Pillar II is worth €52.4 billion. Commissioner for Startups, Research and Innovation Ekaterina Zaharieva and Australia's Minister for Industry and Innovation and Minister for Science, Tim Ayres, signed the text in Brussels.
Under the agreement, Australian researchers and organisations can join and lead international consortia and receive funding on terms similar to those of EU participants. For the rest of the programme nothing changes: Australians keep their access to the parts of the Excellent Science pillar open to non-EU countries, such as the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions, and to the Innovative Europe pillar, depending on the conditions of each call.
Transitional arrangements apply from January 2027. From then, Australian entities can apply to Pillar II calls and be evaluated as prospective beneficiaries. The Commission expects the association to be formally completed by mid-2027, once Australia's parliament has scrutinised it. Negotiations had concluded in June 2026, and Australia is now the 24th country associated with Horizon Europe.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Ullswater Investments analysis: for consortia preparing Pillar II proposals for the 2027 calls, Australian universities, research organisations and companies become partners that can be funded and even lead projects. That makes it easier to add complementary expertise from outside Europe. Because the arrangements are transitional until the association is formally completed, coordinators should check the eligibility wording of each call and keep in close contact with Australian partners as the process moves forward.

## First EDIP Ukraine support call draws 58 defence proposals
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/edip-ukraine-support-call-58-proposals/
Date: 2026-11-11 · Category: EIC, Defence & Equity · Source: European Commission – Defence Industry and Space (https://defence-industry-space.ec.europa.eu/first-usi-ira-call-under-edip-attracts-high-number-proposals-member-states-and-ukraine-2026-11-11_en)

The €184.5 million USI-IRA call on missiles, ammunition and bombs attracted bids from 11 Member States and Ukraine; results are due in March 2027.

- Call: USI-IRA (EDIP Ukraine Support Instrument)
- Proposals: 58, from 11 Member States and Ukraine
- EU funding: €184.5 million
- Per project: Up to €30 million, 100% of eligible costs
- EU-Ukrainian consortia: 59% of proposals
- Results: Planned for March 2027

The first call under the Ukraine Support Instrument of the European Defence Industry Programme (EDIP) closed on 10 November 2026 at 17:00 with 58 proposals, the Commission's Directorate-General for Defence Industry and Space reported. Applicants came from 11 EU Member States and Ukraine.
The call, which covers missiles, ammunition and bombs, aims to increase the capacity of Member States and Ukraine to produce key defence products and their subcomponents. Priority areas include air defence missiles and ammunition, including counter-UxS systems, deep strike capabilities, rockets, bombs and loitering munitions.
Cooperation with Ukrainian industry was strong: 59% of the proposals were submitted by EU-Ukrainian consortia. The call offers €184.5 million in EU funding, with up to €30 million per project and coverage of 100% of eligible costs.
The Commission will now evaluate the proposals and plans to publish results in March 2027. EDIP is a €1.5 billion programme to strengthen Europe's defence industry, and its Ukraine Support Instrument has a dedicated budget of €300 million for the recovery, reconstruction and modernisation of Ukraine's defence technological and industrial base.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): The share of joint EU-Ukrainian bids shows that partnering with Ukrainian manufacturers has become a practical route into EU defence-industrial funding, not just a political goal. With full coverage of eligible costs and large project sizes, these calls suit companies that can expand production capacity quickly. Firms in the defence supply chain that missed this round should track the next EDIP and Ukraine Support Instrument calls and start building cross-border partnerships well before the call opens.

## MEPs back €200 billion Horizon Europe for 2028–2034
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/meps-back-200-billion-horizon-europe-2028-2034/
Date: 2026-11-10 · Category: EU Budget & Policy · Source: European Parliament – Press room (https://www.europarl.europa.eu/news/en/press-room/20261109IPR48713/horizon-europe-meps-back-plans-to-strengthen-the-eu-s-scientific-base)

Parliament's industry and research committee wants €200 billion for the next research programme, above the Commission's €175 billion proposal.

- Committee: Industry, Research and Energy (ITRE)
- Proposed budget: €200 billion in current prices (€177 billion in 2025 prices)
- Commission proposal: €175 billion
- Vote on the regulation: 67 in favour, 1 against, 18 abstentions
- Transfers within pillars: Capped at 10% of the relevant appropriations
- Rapporteurs: Christian Ehler (EPP, DE) and René Repasi (S&D, DE)

The European Parliament's Committee on Industry, Research and Energy has adopted its position on Horizon Europe for 2028–2034, the next EU framework programme for research and innovation. MEPs are asking for €200 billion in current prices, equivalent to €177 billion in 2025 prices, compared with the €175 billion put forward by the Commission. They also want to rework how the programme connects to the proposed European Competitiveness Fund.
On structure, the committee wants to keep the four existing areas of activity: excellent science, competitiveness and society, innovation, and the European Research Area. Each pillar would get its own budget line, and the Commission would only be able to move up to 10% of the relevant appropriations within a pillar. The European Research Council and the European Innovation Council would receive firm budget guarantees and protection of their independence.
MEPs also propose a high-level council of at least 30 independent experts from science, industry and civil society to advise on priorities and help prepare calls for proposals. New schemes would include a 'fast track to excellence', a 'fast track to innovation', support for researchers at risk and similar measures for the social sciences, humanities and arts.
The position on the regulation passed with 67 votes in favour, 1 against and 18 abstentions; the text on the Council Decision passed with 66 in favour, 1 against and 19 abstentions, and the mandate to open negotiations with 65 in favour, 18 against and 2 abstentions. The plenary is expected to confirm the mandate, and talks with member states can only start once the Council has adopted its own position, including the overall figures for the 2028–2034 long-term budget.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): This is not yet the budget applicants will compete for: the final figure depends on negotiations with member states over the whole long-term budget. Still, the Parliament's mandate sets the upper bound of the debate and signals what it will defend, namely separate, protected envelopes for each pillar and for the ERC and EIC. For companies and consortia, the proposed fast-track schemes and the tighter limit on moving money between pillars would make the programme more predictable to plan around. Organisations that want a say should follow the plenary vote and the Council's position over the coming months.
